source.title: Tri-Seal Compliance Note: Cracking Down on Third-Party Intermediaries Used to Evade Russia-Related Sanctions and Export Controls

summary: GOLDEN LABEL, hand-drafted against the PDF. Joint OFAC, BIS and DOJ note on how third-party intermediaries and transshipment points are used to evade Russia-related sanctions and export controls: shell and front companies obscuring ownership and end users, routing through China, Hong Kong, Macau, Armenia, Turkey and Uzbekistan, misdeclared end use, under-stated prices on shipping forms, split shipments, aliases, and rapid onward movement of funds. Names enforcement examples (Milandr network, Vorago Technologies, the Orekhov and Grinin indictments).

citations.quote: One of the most common tactics is the use of third-party intermediaries or transshipment points to circumvent restrictions
Routing purchases through certain transshipment points commonly used to illegally redirect restricted items to Russia or Belarus.
which used a front company to transfer funds from Milandr to another front in a third country, which purchased microchips to divert to Russia.
to Russia via a Bulgarian front company
operation of a network of shell companies designed to enable them to illegally export military and sensitive dual-use items to Russia
disguise the involvement of Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDNs) or parties on the Entity List in transactions, and obscure the true identities of Russian end users.
Use of corporate vehicles (i.e., legal entities, such as shell companies, and legal arrangements) to obscure (i) ownership, (ii) source of funds, or (iii) countries involved
Using aliases for the identities of the intermediaries and end users

Claiming that shell companies located in third countries were intermediaries or end users; in one case, DOJ alleges that only one of the five intermediary parties had any visible signage and consisted of an empty room in a strip mall
Payment coming from a third-party country or business not listed on the End-User Statement
Making false or misleading statements on shipping forms, including underestimating the purchase price of merchandise by more than five times the actual amount
Transferring funds from shell companies in foreign jurisdictions into U.S. bank accounts and quickly forwarding or distributing funds to obfuscate the audit trail or the foreign source of the money
Operation of complex and/or international businesses using residential addresses or addresses common to multiple closely-held corporate entities
a defendant allegedly claimed that an item would be used by Russian space program entities, when in fact the item was suitable for military aircraft or missile systems only

extraction_notes: Golden label. The note names the Alfa Laval Middle East and Nordgas enforcement cases only in footnotes; Sojitz kept as the worked example, the other two left for the reviewer to decide. Ukraine is the victim state, not a risk location, so not in jurisdictions. SAN006 chosen over its TBML twin TBML010 because the note frames everything as sanctions and export-control evasion. Splitting of shipments is NOT BA001 Structuring, which is cash deposits; marked emergent.
